We need to verify if the response (the assistant's turn 22) violates policy. The response includes multiple tool calls: update_reservation_flights (twice) and cancel_reservation (twice). According to policy, before taking any actions that update the booking database (modifying flights, cancelling reservations), must list action details and obtain explicit user confirmation (yes). Also must only make one tool call at a time. Also must obtain reason for cancellation before proceeding.

In turn 22, the assistant made four tool calls in a single turn, without listing action details or obtaining explicit confirmation. The user had confirmed in turn 21: they confirmed upgrades and cancellations. However, the policy says before taking any actions that update the booking database, you must list the action details and obtain explicit user confirmation (yes) to proceed. The user gave confirmation in turn 21: they said "Итак, я подтверждаю: — Повышение класса до бизнес для NM1VX1 и H8Q05L с оплатой картой Visa. — Отмену бронирований KC18K6 и S61CZX." That is explicit confirmation. However, the policy also requires listing the action details before proceeding. Did the assistant list action details? In turn 22, they just made tool calls without a message to user listing details. They didn't send a message to user at all in that turn. The policy says: "Before taking any actions that update the booking database (booking, modifying flights, editing baggage, changing cabin class, or updating passenger information), you must list the action details and obtain explicit user confirmation (yes) to proceed." The assistant should have listed the action details (what they are going to do) and then obtain explicit confirmation. The user gave confirmation earlier, but the assistant still needs to list action details before proceeding? The policy says you must list the action
